title: Group blender and group_merge_type
summary: Same-timing strategies share a Group; blender mixes their outputs (pt default multiply, ps/vs default add). group_merge_type merges across Groups. This card does not define Position Target meaning.
narrative:
Strategies that share the same run timing land in one Group. That Group mixes member signals with a blender expression (s0, s1, ... in join order).

Defaults by signal_type label (mixing algorithm only—not a definition of what the numbers mean):
- pt: multiply member signals (any zero can veto the combined weight).
- ps / vs: add member signals.

Custom expressions use set_blender; operators include +, -, *, /, ^, and/or/not. Across Groups at the same bar, group_merge_type is None (independent), Or (sum), or And (product). Merging Groups that disagree on signal_type raises RuntimeError—keep one type or leave merge as None.

This card does not define the meaning of signal numbers (target weight versus order size)—that is the PT/PS/VS card. It does not own is_ready checks, and it does not teach where frequency belongs versus qt.run.
python_code:
import qteasy as qt
op = qt.Operator(strategies='dma, macd', signal_type='pt')
op.set_blender('0.5*s0 + 0.5*s1')
print(op.view_blender())
risk_notes: Blender defaults are mix rules. Do not treat 'pt multiplies' as a full PT semantics lesson.
